flags.headline: AMD -8.4% on reported AI customer shift to a rival chipmaker plus post-earnings valuation reset
flags.detail: AMD fell 8.4% after a major AI customer was reported to be sourcing AI accelerators from a rival (Nvidia) rather than AMD, compounding an already lukewarm reaction to Tuesday's Q2 print (record $11.5B revenue, +50% YoY, but guidance/beat magnitude fell short of the 'blowout' priced into the stock -- AMD trades ~96% above one fair-value estimate). No single fact here is new information beyond what the market is already pricing, but the combination of a concrete customer-loss data point and a full unwind of the post-earnings pop is a material one-day move on a top-5 sleeve weight.
flags.thesis_link: Matches AMD key_risk: "NVIDIA's 80-90% AI accelerator market share and CUDA software ecosystem dominance -- ROCm's maturity gap creates switching cost risk that could cap AMD's share ceiling." A customer choosing a rival supplier is that risk showing up in a real decision, not just narrative.

evidence.source: Yahoo Finance / AOL (citing Reuters/Bloomberg wire coverage)

flags.headline: HUT down a 2nd straight session (-8.4% today, cumulative ~-17% over two days) as market digests Q2 miss and BTC mark-to-market loss
flags.detail: Hut 8's Q2 revenue jumped 81% YoY but a GAAP net loss of $177M (driven by $138.6M in largely unrealized digital-asset losses) missed consensus on both lines, triggering a -9.7% drop on 8/5 that is still working through the stock today (-8.4%). Underlying AI-infrastructure business metrics remain strong (949MW contracted capacity, ~$26.6B base-term contract value, adjusted EBITDA ex-digital-assets of $10.4M vs $4.2M a year ago), but the market is pricing the bitcoin-treasury volatility, not the AI pivot, this week.
flags.thesis_link: Matches HUT key_risk: "Bitcoin price exposure remains significant... digital asset losses demonstrate the volatility of the crypto treasury strategy." Direct hit for a 2nd consecutive session.

flags.headline: EIX persists RED -- Aug 31 wildfire-liability-reform deadline unchanged, credit-downgrade risk still live
flags.detail: No new escalation today: California lawmakers still have not produced draft wildfire-liability legislation, and CEO Pedro Pizarro's warning that downgrades are 'all but certain' without a durable framework by Aug 31 remains the operative risk. ~$1.6B already committed to wildfire settlements; CPUC has approved $274-650M in Eaton Fire cost recovery from customers. Down another 3.3% today with no fresh catalyst -- continued drift, not a new development.
flags.thesis_link: Matches EIX key_risk: "California's complex regulatory and political environment creates uncertainty around cost recovery, rate base returns, and wildfire liability frameworks that could compress ROE."

flags.headline: CRDO -5.8% in a broad AI-chip-complex pullback following AMD's mixed reaction; no company-specific catalyst
flags.detail: Credo actually saw price-target increases this week (Barclays to $300, Susquehanna to $250) on record FY2026 results -- today's decline tracks the wider chip-sector risk-off following AMD's customer-loss headline, not anything specific to Credo. Grouping with MRVL (-3.6%), LRCX (-3.1%), NXPI (-2.8%), CNX (-3.2%), QCOM (-3.3%), which moved similarly today with no distinct individual catalysts found.

evidence.source: Note: sector-wide move, tier-1 confirmation not required at AMBER per Sentinel guardrails

flags.headline: MRVL -3.6%, part of the same broad AI-chip-complex pullback as CRDO
flags.detail: No distinct MRVL-specific catalyst found; moving with the wider group on AMD-driven capex-sentiment jitters.

flags.headline: DVN -4.5% tracking a broader crude pullback, not a company-specific issue
flags.detail: WTI has fallen >5% over the past two sessions and traded below $76 today on growing optimism a Strait of Hormuz deal could reduce geopolitical risk premium. DVN's own Q2 print (reported 8/4) was strong -- $1.9B net earnings, production gains, plus a $2.6B Delaware Basin acreage acquisition -- and consensus remains Strong Buy with a $59.38 target (+36% from current). This is a commodity-tape move, not a thesis hit.
